newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Editorials-Mar 20.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Editorials-Mar 20.

text.p: There are 103 days to go before the British colony reverts to China. These are highlights of comments in the Hong Kong press. The views expressed are those of the newspapers quoted and do not represent an editorial viewpoint of Reuters.

-- The ECONOMIC JOURNAL said Washington might not grant China Most Favoured Nation (MFN) trading status this year because China had done two unwise things -- getting involved in using money to buy political influence in the United States and scrapping and amending Hong Kong laws. It said Hong Kong's Chief Executive-designate Tung Chee-hwa should talk more about the importance of MFN status to Hong Kong instead of lecturing on how great the territory is on his visit to United States.

-- The Beijing-funded TA KUNG PAO said the Tibetan spiritual leader Dalai Lama's visit to Taiwan was aimed at damaging the prospects for a peaceful reunification between Taiwan and the mainland. It said Taiwan's decision to receive the Dalai Lama would worsen relations between Beijing and Taipei.

-- The English-language SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST said Beijing had extricated itself with great skill from the problem posed by the defection of North Korean official Hwang Jang-yop. After five weeks of intensive negotiations, the situation was solved with a minimum of damage to relations between Beijing and Seoul and Pyongyang.
